newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Europe grain crop needs lasting rainfall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Europe grain crop needs lasting rainfall.

text.p: Forecasts of rain for western Europe will be welcomed by farmers but it needs to be sustained to benefit crop growth.
"The trouble is, the ground's so dry that a lot of it will evaporate straightaway," one farming source in eastern England said.

"We need as much as possible," she said. Rain was needed not just for crops in the ground, but also, and in much bigger quantities, to replenish farmers' reservoirs, which were at a low level after a dry winter, she said.
But spring sown crops could benefit even from a small amount of rain, "because they went into such dry seedbeds," she said.

In France, scattered rain is expected over the weekend, but it will not be enough to bring much relief to thirsty crops after a three-month dry spell, the national meteorological service Meteo France said on Thursday.
"We are expecting scattered showers but they are unlikely to bring much relief," Meteo forecaster Franck Baraer told Reuters.
"We would need 15 days of rain to help improve the situation," he said.
On Friday light rain will hit western France from Caen to Toulouse. Scattered showers will reach the north and the southeast on Saturday.
"There is a chance of more substantial rain in the southern part of the country on Saturday," he said.
But by Sunday only eastern France will experience some rain.
The important English cereal producing area of East Anglia, hardest hit by the dry weather, is likely to get some rain during the course of Friday, a spokesman for the Meteorological Office said.

A second belt of rain will cross the country on Sunday, followed by showers next week, the spokesman said. Showery conditions, however, are more likely to benefit the north and west, than the south and east.
"There is a change in the weather pattern over the next five days," he said.
"The difficult question is still the amount of rain," he said. But the indications were that "most parts will see measurable rain, rather than the spots we've seen over the past few days."
In Italy, drought conditions have been to some extent eased by rainfall in recent days, although alarm over frost continues.

Unseasonal weather conditions, with drought in northern Italy, rain in the south and frost throughout the country, have caused serious damage to crops, the Italian national farmers' federation Coldiretti said.
It noted that the inclement conditions this spring, following particularly mild weather at the end of winter, were still continuing.
Italian farm minister Michele Pinto said on Thursday that the government was ready to help out areas of the country where crops have been badly hit.
German crops are suffering from chilly day temperatures and late night frosts but rains will soon ease an accompanying dry spell, the national meteorological office DWD said.
"German crops do not need as much rain as those damaged by drought further west and south in Europe, because there was good precipitation in February," a DWD source said.
